title: RTL2MμPATH: Multi-μPATH Synthesis with Applications to Hardware Security Verification
problem: Prior work RTL2μSPEC assumes instructions can exhibit only a single microarchitectural execution path, limiting its applicability to realistic processors where instructions like loads have multiple paths (e.g., cache hit/miss). The verification gap between manually-written μSPEC models and actual RTL implementations hinders broad adoption of formal processor security verification.
motivation: Automating the synthesis of formally verified microarchitectural specifications from processor RTL is essential for scaling hardware security verification and defending against microarchitectural side-channel attacks.
method: RTL2MμPATH automatically discovers formally verified microarchitectural execution paths (μPATHS) for each instruction from System Verilog designs given instruction encodings and design metadata. SYnthlc extends RTL2MμPATH by applying symbolic information flow analysis to synthesize and formally verify leakage contracts—specifications of what information microarchitectural side channels may leak—directly against the RTL implementation.
key_novelty: First automated methodology to formally verify hardware adherence to leakage contracts by recognizing that instructions with multiple execution paths strongly indicate microarchitectural side channels.
contributions: RTL2MμPATH tool that removes the single-execution-path assumption and automatically synthesizes formally verified microarchitectural paths for instructions with multiple behaviors
Observation that multi-path instructions strongly indicate microarchitectural side channels
SYnthlc tool extending RTL2MμPATH with symbolic information flow analysis to synthesize formally verified leakage contracts
First automated approach for formal verification of hardware adherence to leakage contracts
limitations: Evaluation scope, scalability to large designs, and approach limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Automated microarchitectural path synthesis for hardware security verification
